gist: Atwood argues that the ancient adepts and Theurgists reached the captive inner Light by patient, rational, experimental inquiry, in which natural reason is only an 'iron key' and the real agent of the work is a freed spiritual Intellect, the 'true Separator'. The Hermetic Separation is identified with the death-and-resurrection ordeals of the Mysteries, and the chunk closes with Anaxagoras on Intellect as the unmingled power that separates all things.

notes.point: Physicians of the middle periods freed this Light to cure the body. The Theurgic Art went further and purified the Mind, nearest to Christ's doctrine of regeneration: baptismal purification, then gradual subjugation of the passions to reason, until the whole hypostasis was converted through faith into substant light within.

The ancients sought this Reason by questioning Nature rationally, not by demolishing her as modern chemistry does. Admitted from within as lawful guests, they did not collect phenomena for private judgment but addressed nature in her own light, to become worthy of it.
Theurgists consulted the divine intellect only on purification, liberation and salvation of life, and on things tending to discover truth.

Every beginner wanders first among chimeras and makes many erroneous inquiries. Rightly begun, investigation traces the chain of vital causes to Deity and, under the divine will, works supernatural perfection below. The aim was the Central Light, until the hidden Divinity became manifest in experience.

Alchemists: examine patiently and infer from experience by God's Rule. Help nature beyond her common course, because the Mercury of the Wise comes only by ingenuity and industry. Crollius: holy, assiduous preparation, contemplation and handiwork, with grace, bring forth more than nature promises. Van Helmont: the Tree of Life is laborious intellectual research. Basil Valentine: find nature's concealed first foundation with your own eyes and hand, or build on sand.
notes.voice: QUOTED: Alchemists; Crollius; Van Helmont; Basil Valentine (endorsed)

notes.point: All adepts (Lully, Maier and others) agree that the way to Wisdom is patience and rational inquiry into intimate causes, aimed at entering the fundamental experience.

Basil: the second part is celestial contemplation by spiritual reason. It shows how nature is perfected by resolution of itself, and how destruction and compaction are handled to separate pure from impure.

Natural reason is necessary but inoperative here, an iron key unlocking the inner treasury of light. Once it brings the spiritual intellect into self-knowledge, that intellect turns on the outer life and proves all 'chemically' by its new Law. This vital perscrutinator (Eirenaeus: 'internal fire of the sulfur of thy water') works the whole change. Only those with this passport pass the narrow gate, as in the Mysteries. The thing sought is the flower of intellect, triply imprisoned in the body, and only a lover of Wisdom can free it.

Eirenaeus: our fire, the sulfur of Gold, is imprisoned in the hard body and loosed by our water rotting the body's 'moles' (glossed: the ethereal body). It appears in the Third Menstrual, which is inaccessible without the first two. Prepare the first water, join it to the body in just pondus, seal it until the infant forms, keep external heat cherishing internal, and wait for signs: the body's pores open and the tincture of Sol is partly extracted. Heed the internal Fire over the Athanor's. Seek it in Aries and Saturn; the signal is the Doves of Diana.

Parallels: the Sybil sends Aeneas for the Golden Bough, which yields only to one the fates call. Orpheus's Cave of Mercury is, per the Hermetic interpretation, Taenerus, the most hidden vapor of life. A prudent seeker, allied to what he seeks, carries off the mineral radix. Without a right mind and the predestined order of operation, the power stays hidden in an uncongenial soul.
Fire loves fire, to assimilate gold rather than make it. Throw the true gold-body, not a brazen ferment, into a bottomless Mercury.

The art of Oedipus subdues the Sphinx: the Ethereal Spirit drops her phantasy and yields understanding to the trained investigator. Synesius: Intellect purifies the phantastic Spirit and extends it to Divinity. Natural intellect cannot. Atwood concedes that language fails to convey the freed will acting on its vehicle and transmuting it to universal intelligence, but resolves to explain this Intellectual Science.

The Separation that Paracelsus calls philosophy's greatest miracle is identical with the Mysteries' death of the natural life: suffering, dread, dissolution and corruption, then the resurrection of pure Ether into Light. It is the Art's primary object. The creature has free power in it, and the sequestratrix that gives form and essence is Intellect, Hermes's perscrutinating Intellect ('Separabis').

The decomposition is not mechanical. Mind is the true Separator and regimen, and no foreign admixture enters. Nothing is discovered without decomposing the matter or perfected without the whole introversion. The matter is One Thing (Hermes), of which phantasy, folly, passion and Reason are modes. Reason, prevailing, gathers all as a ferment into its Light, as the Head Stone writers intimate.

Ordinary reason, which separates fact from falsehood and governs the passions, is the image of this higher Reason. The ancients call it Wisdom, Intellect, Gold, Sol, Sulfur and Tincture. Like the sun, this Intellectual sun purifies, separates false forms, triturates foreign tincture and infuses itself into the passified Spirit.

Anaxagoras (via Simplicius and Taylor): Intellect is infinite, unmingled, alone and most pure. It knows and rules all and separated dense from rare, hot from cold, lucid from dark and dry from moist. Only Intellect is singular by itself.

method.veiled: To find this Light, and to free it from captivity
method.plain: The object of the work is a light held captive, which must be found and released.
method.basis: ¶11 locates the light 'within' ('substant light within'); ¶13 speaks of 'the golden treasury of light within' and 'the flower of human intellect, triply imprisoned in the dark body’s hold', which the philosopher must 'open and set free'.

method.veiled: by an effectual baptismal purification, they also prepared the way
method.plain: The Theurgic Art began with a purification that prepared the way for what followed.
method.basis: ¶11 states the sequence directly.

method.veiled: by a gradual subjugation of the passions and adaptation of the subordinate powers to reason
method.plain: The passions are mastered step by step, and the lower faculties are brought into line with reason.

method.veiled: the whole hypostasis was converted finally through faith into the identity of substant light within
method.plain: In the end the whole person is turned, through faith, into identity with the inner light.
method.basis: ¶11. 'Hypostasis' is read as 'the whole being' because the conversion is of 'the whole'; this chunk does not define the word.

method.veiled: they knocked as was bid them, and the doors being opened from within, they enjoyed and took advantage of their entrance as lawful guests
method.plain: Nature is approached by rational, respectful questioning, and entry is granted from inside rather than forced, unlike modern chemistry.
method.basis: ¶12 contrasts this with modern chemistry that would 'demolish her edifices and burn her out of life and home', and opens with 'put the question to Nature rationally'.

method.veiled: they consulted it about things which pertain to purification, liberation, as Iamblicus tells us, and the salvation of life
method.plain: The divine intellect is consulted only about purification, liberation and salvation, never about trifles.

method.veiled: he wanders awhile in the region of chimeras
method.plain: Every beginner first goes through a period of many, often mistaken inquiries before reaching experimental knowledge.
method.basis: ¶13: 'the inquiries which he makes before attaining to experimental knowledge are many, and often erroneous'.

method.veiled: having set the chain of vital causes in action, succeeded in tracing them to their last efficient link in Deity
method.plain: The adepts set a series of living causes working and followed it up to its first cause in God, from which they could then work effects 'below'.
method.basis: ¶13: 'whence surveying, they were enabled, under the divine will, to work such perfection in things below'.

method.veiled: you must help her, that she may exceed her common course
method.plain: Nature alone does not produce the result. The operator must assist her past her ordinary course.
method.basis: ¶13: 'Seek not for that in nature which is an effect beyond her strength'.

method.veiled: the Mercury of the Wise comes not but by help of ingenuity and industry
method.plain: The needed 'Mercury' is not found ready-made. It is obtained only through the operator's skill and labour.
method.basis: ¶13 states the condition. What the Mercury of the Wise is, this chunk does not say.

method.veiled: a holy assiduity of preparations, joining thereto diligent contemplation of natural causes
method.plain: The operator needs devout, persistent preparatory work, contemplation of causes and hands-on labour, and success also depends on infused grace.
method.basis: ¶13 (Crollius): 'shall refuse no pains or difficulties to get experience by the industry of his handy work... if the grace of the most high be infused into him'.

method.veiled: Learn and look for the first foundation, says the monk, which nature holds concealed
method.plain: Nature hides a first foundation, and the operator must find it by direct experience ('thine own eyes and hand').

method.veiled: how nature may be helped and perfected by resolution of itself, and how the destruction and compaction are to be handled
method.plain: The work perfects nature by dissolving it into itself and managing a destroying phase and a consolidating phase, so that pure separates from impure. Only spiritual reason grasps this.
method.basis: ¶13: 'whereby... the pure may be separated from the impure'; 'to be understood with spiritual reason'.

method.veiled: as it were an iron key, intended to unlock the golden treasury of light within
method.plain: Ordinary natural reason is a necessary but merely preliminary tool. It opens access to the inner light and does not itself do the work.
method.basis: ¶13: natural reason 'is dull here comparatively, and inoperative, and stands... albeit necessary, as a mere circumstantial aid on the threshold'.

method.veiled: this latter, returning with power upon the life without, proceeds to analyze and revolutionize
method.plain: Once natural reason has opened the way, a spiritual intellect comes to know itself and then acts outward, analyzing and transforming the outer life.
method.basis: ¶13: natural reason first 'helped to introduce the spiritual intellect into self-knowledge'; 'this latter' then proves all 'by the fiery essence of its newly conceived Law'.

method.veiled: the internal fire of the sulfur of thy water
method.plain: Eirenaeus's phrase for the 'vital perscrutinator', the searching inner agent that carries out the whole change. In context this is the self-knowing spiritual intellect just described.
method.basis: ¶13 says outright that the vital perscrutinator, 'the internal fire of the sulfur of thy water, as Eirenaeus calls it', 'operates the whole change'. Equating it with the spiritual intellect rests on the preceding sentence and on ¶20–21, where Intellect is the separating agent.

method.veiled: they only, literally speaking, can enter in through the narrow gate
method.plain: Only those who have the 'passport', the awakened inner agent, can reach the Magistery. This bars intruders.
method.basis: ¶13: 'they only who have obtained this passport can attain to the Magistery of life'; compared to the Mysteries.

method.veiled: the flower of human intellect, triply imprisoned in the dark body’s hold
method.plain: What is sought is the highest part of the human intellect, locked deep within the body, and the philosopher must free it.
method.basis: ¶13: 'This it is the business of the philosopher to open and set free'. The meaning of 'triply' is not explained.

method.veiled: he must be a lover of Wisdom who can set her free
method.plain: Only a true lover of Wisdom can free what is imprisoned. This requirement is itself the safeguard.
method.basis: ¶13: 'this is the security'.

method.veiled: Our fire is the true sulfur of Gold
method.plain: The active fire of the work is the 'sulfur of Gold', imprisoned in a hard, dry body and released through 'our water'.
method.basis: ¶14. It links to ¶13's 'internal fire of the sulfur of thy water', the vital perscrutinator.

method.veiled: by rotting the moles of the body (i.e., of the ethereal body)
method.plain: The water frees the fire by putrefying the masses that hold it, and a parenthetical gloss says these belong to the ethereal body.
method.basis: ¶14. The parenthetical glosses '(i.e., of the ethereal body)' and '(of the same body)' sit inside the quotation and appear to be Atwood's insertions. 'Moles' is read as 'masses' from the context of a body that detains the fire.
method.voice: QUOTED: Eirenaeus, with gloss probably by ATWOOD

method.veiled: it appears visibly in our Third Menstrual
method.plain: After the elements of the body separate, the freed fire becomes visible at a third stage or solvent, which can be reached only through the first two ('menstruals').
method.basis: ¶14: 'he that knows not our two first menstruals is altogether shut out from attaining to the sight of this Third and last'.

method.veiled: to prepare the first water, and to join it to the body in a just pondus
method.plain: Prepare the first water and join it to the body in the right proportion.
method.basis: ¶14. 'Pondus' is read as weight or proportion; the text does not gloss it.

method.veiled: to shut it up in its vessel philosophically, until the infant be formed
method.plain: Seal the compound in its vessel 'philosophically' and leave it until something new (the 'infant') has formed.
method.basis: ¶14. What the vessel and infant stand for is not stated in this chunk.

method.veiled: to govern his fire dexterously, so as to cherish internal heat with external
method.plain: The chief skill is regulating the heat so that the outer heat sustains the inner heat.
method.basis: ¶14 calls this 'what is greater than all'.

method.veiled: can wait with patience till he sees signs
method.plain: The operator waits patiently for visible signs. The first is that the water opens the body's pores and partly draws out the tincture of Sol.

method.veiled: opened the pores and extracted partly the tincture of Sol
method.plain: The first water acts on the body until it is opened and part of its 'tincture of Sol' (its gold-principle) is extracted.
method.basis: ¶14. ¶21 lists 'Gold, Sol, Sulfur, Tincture' among the ancients' names for the Reason or Intellect, which supports reading 'tincture of Sol' as that principle.

method.veiled: be not so careful of the fire of the Athanor as of your internal Fire
method.plain: The furnace's outer fire matters less than the inner fire.
method.basis: ¶14. It is consistent with ¶13, where the internal fire 'operates the whole change'.

method.veiled: Seek it in the house of Aries, and draw it from the depths of Saturn; let Mercury be the internal, and your signal the Doves of Diana
method.plain: Directions on where to seek the internal Fire and what sign to watch for. This chunk gives no key to these astrological and mythological names.
method.basis: ¶14 only. See ambiguities.

method.veiled: well directing him how to look from beneath upwards, and take it in hand
method.plain: As with the Golden Bough, the seeker searches upward through obscurity and takes the thing in hand. It yields freely only to one the fates call; force cannot win it.
method.basis: ¶15 and ¶16 ('Si te fate vocant; aliter, non viribus ullis Vincere'); Atwood presents it as 'some such errand'.

method.veiled: the Cave of Mercury, which, according to the Hermetic interpretation, is Taenerus, the most hidden vapor of life
method.plain: The 'cave' where the goods are found is the most hidden vapour of life.

method.veiled: the mineral radix and true mater of the Hermetic Art
method.plain: What the rightly disposed seeker brings out of the Cave of Mercury is the root and true matter of the Art.

method.veiled: let him enter with a prudent motive, well understanding and allied to what he seeks
method.plain: The seeker must have a prudent motive and real understanding, and must be akin to what he seeks.

method.veiled: the power will remain hidden, despite of every effort, in a pusillanimous uncongenial soul
method.plain: Without a right mind and observance of the predestined conditions and order of operation, no effort succeeds. A faint-hearted, unsuited soul cannot bring out the power.
method.basis: ¶19: 'if he have not a right mind, and unless the predestined conditions and the order of operation be observed, all will be in vain'.

method.veiled: Fire loves fire, say they, not to make gold, but to assimilate it
method.plain: The active fire does not manufacture gold. It assimilates what it acts on into its own nature.
method.basis: ¶19. Compare ¶21: Reason 'would gather all up, as a ferment, into the superior essence' and supernatural reason works by 'assimilating the whole inferior life'.

method.veiled: Take, therefore, that body which is gold (not a brazen ferment), and throw it into Mercury
method.plain: Put the true gold-body, not a false or base ferment, into a 'bottomless' Mercury, where it finds the Mercury's centre only by discovering its own.
method.basis: ¶19: 'such a Mercury as is bottomless, or whose center it can never find, but by discovering its own'. What the gold-body and Mercury refer to is not stated here.
method.voice: QUOTED: "they" (Ripley Revived; Maier; Lumen de Lumine), endorsed

method.veiled: This is the art of Oedipus which, well conducted with the Sphinx, ends in her subjugation
method.plain: The work subdues the Ethereal Spirit. It gives up its fantasy and yields clear understanding to a properly trained investigator.
method.basis: ¶20: 'in other words, the Ethereal Spirit abandons her phantasy, and yields the clear light of understanding to him who... knows how and wherewith to investigate her peculiar essence'.

method.veiled: Intellect above all things separates whatever is contrary to the true purity of phantastic Spirit
method.plain: Intellect purifies the imaginal ('phantastic') spirit, refining it hiddenly and extending it to Divinity. Natural intellect cannot do this.
method.basis: ¶20: 'But the natural Intellect cannot do this'.

method.veiled: the efficient force of an individual freed will upon the vehicle of its motive cause
method.plain: The adepts claimed that a freed individual will acts on its own vehicle, separating, refining and transmuting it from an impure, dull state into clear universal intelligence.
method.basis: ¶20: 'separating, refining, and transmuting it from an impure, dull consistency to the clear light of universal intelligence'.

method.veiled: Separation is the greatest miracle in philosophy
method.plain: Separation is the primary object of the Art. It is the same as the ordeal of the Mysteries: the decomposition and death of the natural life, ending in the pure Ether's resurrection into Light.
method.basis: ¶21: 'appears to be identical with that which is described as taking place in the Mysteries'; 'This Separation is indeed the primary object of the Art'.

method.veiled: from the beginning in suffering, succedent dread, dissolution, and corruption, to the final resurrection of the pure Ether into Light
method.plain: The stages of Separation run in order: suffering, then dread, dissolution, corruption, and finally the rising of the purified Ether as Light.

method.veiled: that is the sequestatrix, which gives to every thing its form and essence
method.plain: The separating power that gives things their form and essence is Intellect.
method.basis: ¶21: 'which is the part especial of Intellect, that same perscrutinating Intellect which Hermes speaks of'.

method.veiled: there is a free power in the creature to its mutual affection and destruction
method.plain: Separation is not God's work alone. The creature has a free power in it, and free will can help or hinder the work.
method.basis: ¶21: 'if it were divinely done by God alone, it would be to no purpose to study after it'; 'The free will... is either friend or foe in our works'.

method.veiled: Thou shalt separate the earth from the fire, the subtle from the gross, gently, with much sagacity
method.plain: Separate subtle from gross gently and wisely. The separated thing ascends and descends and gains the strength of both superiors and inferiors.
method.basis: ¶21, n22 (Smaragdine Tablet); Atwood reads 'Separabis' as the work of Intellect.

method.veiled: we observe Mind to be the true Separator, the efficient as well as the regimen of the work
method.plain: Mind both does the separating and governs the conduct of the work. The decomposition is not mechanical or ordinary.
method.basis: ¶21: 'Nor ought we... to understand this decomponency of life in a mechanical sense'.

method.veiled: no foreign admixture is allowed to enter
method.plain: Nothing foreign may be added to the work.
method.basis: ¶21 ('as before shown'). Compare ¶13: 'it is no graft from this life that enters into the divine foundation'.

method.veiled: nothing is discovered except the matte be decomposed, and because it is not perfected unless the whole introversion is passed through
method.plain: Nothing is found until the matter is decomposed, and nothing is perfected until a complete turning-inward has run its course.

method.veiled: the whole matter I know to be One only Thing
method.plain: The matter of the work is one single thing, of which folly, phantasy, passion and Reason are different modes.
method.basis: ¶21, n24; the next sentence: 'folly, and phantasy, and passion are modes of being of the One Thing, and Reason is another'.

method.veiled: this Reason gaining the ascendancy, would gather all up, as a ferment, into the superior essence and traction of her own Light
method.plain: If Reason gains ascendancy within the one matter, it works like leaven and draws the whole into its own light. If phantasy prevails, everything turns to folly.

method.veiled: so are we taught to conceive of the Intellectual sun
method.plain: The higher Reason or Intellect acts on the inner life as the sun acts on matter, purifying, subliming and converting.
method.basis: ¶21: 'as the luminary of the sensible world purifies and subtilizes the gross parts of matter... so are we taught to conceive of the Intellectual sun'.

method.veiled: assimilating the whole inferior life by continual trituration of its foreign tincture
method.plain: Supernatural reason rejects the false forms acquired through generation, wears away the foreign colouring of the lower life to assimilate it, and perfects the faculties by pouring itself into the passive Spirit.
method.basis: ¶21: 'separating and rejecting the false forms and elementary qualities which supervene through generation... by pure infusion of Itself to the passified Spirit throughout'.

method.veiled: Intellect is infinite and possesses absolute power, and is not mingled with any thing; but is alone by itself
method.plain: Intellect can separate and rule all things only because it is itself unmixed. It separates dense from rare, hot from cold, lucid from dark, dry from moist.
method.basis: ¶22; Atwood cites it in ¶21 as confirming Intellect's 'efficient operation'.

terms.meaning: The captive inner light that the work seeks to find and free. The Theurgic Art converts the whole person into identity with it. Reason or Intellect is called Light.

equivalences.quote: For it is Light indeed, and an occult splendor of existence transcendentally pure

quotes.text: To find this Light, and to free it from captivity
For the Central Light and Wisdom was all their aim

terms.meaning: An art claiming to purify and inform the Mind, beyond healing the body. It proceeds by baptismal purification and subjugation of the passions to reason, and consults the divine intellect only on purification, liberation and salvation.

quotes.text: the Theurgic Art professed a power of purifying and informing the Mind much more beneficial and lasting than this pertaining to the mortal body

terms.meaning: Used for the whole that is converted into the inner light. The chunk gives no definition. n26 mentions a treatise 'on the Gnostic Hypostasis'.

quotes.text: the whole hypostasis was converted finally through faith into the identity of substant light within

equivalences.quote: it is of this the ancients speak, calling it Wisdom, Intellect, Gold, Sol, Sulfur, Tincture

this Reason gaining the ascendancy, would gather all up, as a ferment, into the superior essence and traction of her own Light

equivalences.quote: as it were an iron key, intended to unlock the golden treasury of light within

But the natural Intellect cannot do this, neither comprehending properly, or being conceived of the Spirit

quotes.text: this latter, returning with power upon the life without, proceeds to analyze and revolutionize

terms.meaning: The searching inner agent that 'operates the whole change'. Eirenaeus calls it the internal fire of the sulfur of thy water, and Atwood links it to the perscrutinating Intellect of Hermes.

equivalences.with: internal fire of the sulfur of thy water
equivalences.quote: It is this vital perscrutinator, the internal fire of the sulfur of thy water, as Eirenaeus calls it

equivalences.quote: that is the sequestatrix, which gives to every thing its form and essence (20); which is the part especial of Intellect

quotes.text: no one thing is singular by itself except Intellect

terms.meaning: The primary object of the Art and its greatest miracle. It is identical with the Mysteries' decomposition and death of the natural life, ending in the resurrection of pure Ether into Light, and it is effected by Mind or Intellect.

equivalences.quote: appears to be identical with that which is described as taking place in the Mysteries, when the great ordeals are passed through during the decomposition and death of the natural life

quotes.text: This Separation is indeed the primary object of the Art

terms.meaning: What the Alchemists 'distil'. The pure Ether rises as Light at the end of Separation. The Ethereal Spirit, likened to the Sphinx, gives up her phantasy under the right investigation. A parenthetical gloss says the body whose 'moles' are rotted is the ethereal body.

quotes.text: But what say our Oedipus distillers of this Ether, the instructive Alchemists?
the Ethereal Spirit abandons her phantasy, and yields the clear light of understanding

terms.meaning: The image-making mode of the Spirit and of the One Thing. If it prevails, it converts the inner life to folly. Intellect separates what is contrary to the purity of the phantastic Spirit.

quotes.text: as the phantasy, if suffered to prevail, will convert all to her own folly in the internal life

terms.meaning: The single matter of the work. Folly, phantasy, passion and Reason are all its modes.

quotes.text: the whole matter I know to be One only Thing
folly, and phantasy, and passion are modes of being of the One Thing, and Reason is another

terms.meaning: The Hermetic operation. Natural reason stands in it only as a threshold aid, and Mind is its Separator and regimen.

quotes.text: stands in the Philosophic Work, albeit necessary, as a mere circumstantial aid on the threshold of the divine inquiry

terms.meaning: A complete inward turning that must be passed through before the work is perfected.

quotes.text: it is not perfected unless the whole introversion is passed through

terms.meaning: That which, according to the Asclepius, man can find and also effect.

quotes.text: man should be able not only to find the Causal Nature but to effect it

terms.meaning: Atwood's name for the doctrine of the magic action of mind and the freed will on its vehicle, which she undertakes to 'substantialize without deforming'.

quotes.text: to substantialize without deforming this Intellectual Science

variants: Rule which God hath given thee
terms.meaning: The God-given standard for discerning right from wrong. 'The Reason of our Rule' is the superior Reason, the archetype of that standard.

quotes.text: Take hold of that Rule which God hath given thee for direction, by which thou mayest discern the right from the wrong

terms.meaning: Its attainment is laborious and the fruit of intellectual research.

quotes.text: the attainment of the Tree of Life is laborious, and the fruit of intellectual research

terms.meaning: The perfect doctrine preached by Jesus Christ and his apostles. The Theurgic Art came nearer to fulfilling it than any other known art.

quotes.text: a fulfillment of the perfect doctrine of regeneration preached by Jesus Christ and his apostles

terms.meaning: Their ordeals of decomposition and death of the natural life are identical with the Hermetic Separation. Their 'narrow gate' admits only those who are qualified.

quotes.text: can enter in through the narrow gate, as in the Mysteries we have already described

sources.name: Jesus Christ and his apostles
sources.use: Supports: the Theurgic Art came nearest to fulfilling their 'perfect doctrine of regeneration'.

sources.name: Iamblicus
sources.use: Supports: Theurgists consulted the divine intellect only about purification, liberation and the salvation of life.

sources.name: Vaughan
sources.use: Reference for the beginner's erroneous inquiries; also cited for the alchemists' counsel (n11) and the 'Fire loves fire' passage (n18).

sources.name: B.. Valentine
sources.use: Reference only, for the beginner's erroneous inquiries.

sources.name: Norton
sources.use: Reference only, for the beginner's erroneous inquiries.

sources.name: Lully
sources.work: Lullii Theoria et Practica, cap. 68 and 88; Arbor Scientiae, Brancha Human; Lullii Arbor 10, Scientiae, p. 99
sources.quote: Intellectus naturam habens subtilem ad intelligendum res intelligibles
sources.use: Supports: the alchemists' counsel on patient inquiry; the way to Wisdom by patience; the doctrine of Reason as ferment and Head Stone; the description of Intellect.

sources.name: Crollius
sources.quote: come to the inner rooms of nature by a holy assiduity of preparations
sources.use: Supports: preparation, contemplation, hands-on labour and grace bring forth more than nature promises.

sources.name: Van Helmont
sources.quote: the attainment of the Tree of Life is laborious, and the fruit of intellectual research
sources.use: Supports: the work is laborious intellectual research.

sources.name: Basil Valentine
sources.quote: Learn and look for the first foundation, says the monk, which nature holds concealed
sources.use: Supports: seek the hidden foundation by direct experience. The second part of his admonition is celestial and understood by spiritual reason, separating pure from impure.

sources.name: Michael Maier
sources.use: Cited as an example of patient rational inquiry and as a reference for the 'Fire loves fire' passage.

sources.name: Eirenaeus
sources.quote: Our fire is the true sulfur of Gold
sources.use: Supports: names the inner agent ('internal fire of the sulfur of thy water') and gives the process of the three menstruals, the first water, the vessel, the fire regimen and the signs.

sources.name: the poet
sources.use: Illustrates: the thing sought is hidden far off.

sources.name: the Sybil / Aeneas
sources.quote: Alte vestiga oculis: et rite repertum, Carpe manu
sources.use: Illustrates: the search for the Golden Bough as a parallel errand. It yields only to one the fates call.

sources.name: Orpheus
sources.use: Illustrates: entering the Cave of Mercury with prudence of heart to carry off its goods, read by Atwood in the Hermetic interpretation.

sources.name: Synesius
sources.work: de Somniis (extract in Taylor’s Proculus on Euclid)
sources.quote: Intellect above all things separates whatever is contrary to the true purity of phantastic Spirit
sources.use: Supports: Intellect purifies and extends the phantastic Spirit to Divinity.

sources.name: Paracelsus
sources.work: his book to the Athenians; First Book of the Athenians, text 9, 10
sources.quote: Separation is the greatest miracle in philosophy
sources.use: Supports: Separation as the primary object, the free power of the creature, free will as friend or foe, and the sequestratrix.

sources.name: Hermes
sources.work: Tract. Aureus, cap. 2 and cap. 4; Smagardine Tablet (Tabula Smaragdina hermetis); Asclepius (Aclepius, cap. 13)
sources.quote: Separabis, Thou shalt separate the earth from the fire, the subtle from the gross
sources.use: Supports: the perscrutinating Intellect as Separator; the whole matter is One Thing; man can find and effect the Causal Nature.

sources.name: Arnold
sources.use: Cited as celebrating the Head Stone.

sources.name: Bacon
sources.use: Cited as celebrating the Head Stone.

sources.name: Geber
sources.use: Cited as celebrating the Head Stone.

sources.name: Manget
sources.use: Reference only, on the Head Stone.

sources.name: Plotinus
sources.work: Select Works, treatise on the Gnostic Hypostasis
sources.use: Reference: 'a very beautiful treatise', cited alongside Lully on Intellect.

sources.name: Anaxagoras
sources.work: lost works, preserved by Simplicius, given in a note to Aristotle’s Metaphysics by Taylor
sources.quote: Intellect is infinite and possesses absolute power, and is not mingled with any thing
sources.use: Supports: confirms Intellect's efficient, separating operation. Atwood calls him 'one of the earliest of the Greek hermetic School'.

sources.name: Simplicius
sources.use: Transmitter of the Anaxagoras passage.

sources.name: Taylor
sources.work: note to Aristotle’s Metaphysics; Taylor’s Proculus on Euclid
sources.use: Translator or editor through whom the Anaxagoras and Synesius passages are given.

sources.name: modern chemistry
sources.quote: to demolish her edifices and burn her out of life and home
sources.use: Criticized: a rude interrogation of Nature, contrasted with the ancients' rational inquiry.

ambiguities.quote: Seek it in the house of Aries, and draw it from the depths of Saturn; let Mercury be the internal, and your signal the Doves of Diana
readings: Literal astrological or chemical directions for where to find the internal Fire.
Veiled names for inner conditions or stages of the work. The chunk gives no key, only that the Fire sought is 'internal'.
ambiguities.basis: ¶14 offers no gloss. The immediately preceding contrast between Athanor fire and 'internal Fire' favours some inward reference, but the specific terms are unexplained.

ambiguities.quote: Salt is good, but if the Salt have lost its savor wherewith shall it be seasoned?
readings: Natural intellect, lacking penetrative essence, cannot season or transform the Spirit, so a higher Intellect is needed.
A warning that if the Intellect or agent itself is corrupted, nothing can restore the work.
ambiguities.basis: It follows directly on 'the natural Intellect cannot do this... neither is its essence so acutely penetrative as to operate the change required' (¶20).

ambiguities.quote: such a Mercury as is bottomless, or whose center it can never find, but by discovering its own
readings: 'it' is the gold-body, which can find Mercury's centre only by discovering its own centre.
'it' is the Mercury, which never finds its centre except by self-discovery.
ambiguities.basis: The grammar of ¶19 permits either. The sentence's subject is the gold thrown into Mercury.

ambiguities.quote: that which he shall bear away from thence, Centaur-like, in both his Hands
readings: 'Both hands' simply renders the Latin 'Ambabus... minibus' (¶18): he carries away a great amount.
'Centaur-like' implies a double, man-and-beast nature in the bearer. The chunk does not explain it.
ambiguities.basis: ¶18 Latin has 'Ambabus valet hic minibus sibi sumere'. 'Centaur-like' is Atwood's addition and is not glossed.

ambiguities.quote: But the contemplation which absolves the Second part of our admonition is celestial
readings: The 'first part' is the earlier advice to search the foundation with eyes and hand (experience); the second is spiritual contemplation.
It refers to a division in Basil's text not reproduced here.
ambiguities.basis: ¶13 earlier quotes Basil on searching 'with thine own eyes and hand'; n14 'Disce igitur, etc.' and n15 'Chariot of Antimony' are different citations.

ambiguities.quote: triply imprisoned in the dark body’s hold
readings: Three specific enclosures. This might connect with the three menstruals of ¶14, but the chunk does not say so.
ambiguities.basis: No explanation of 'triply' is given in ¶13 or ¶14.

ambiguities.quote: by rotting the moles of the body (i.e., of the ethereal body)
readings: 'moles' means masses or bulk of the body.
The parenthetical glosses are Atwood's insertions redirecting the reading to an 'ethereal body', rather than Eirenaeus's own words.
ambiguities.basis: The parentheticals appear inside an attributed quotation (¶14) and are probably editorial, but the text does not mark them as such.

translations.translation: hidden away, it sits further off

translations.original: Alte vestiga oculis: et rite repertum, Carpe manu; namque Ipse volens facilisaque sequetur, Si te fate vocant; aliter, non viribus ullis Vincere, nec duro poteris convellere ferro
translations.translation: Search on high with your eyes, and when duly found, pluck it with your hand; for of itself it will follow, willing and easy, if the fates call you; otherwise you will not be able to overcome it by any strength, nor tear it away with hard iron.

translations.original: At quaecunque virum ducit prudnetia cordis Mercurii ingedier spuluncam plurima ubi ille Deponit bona, stat quorum praegrandis acervus Ambabus valet hic minibus sibi sumere, et ista Ferre domum, valet hic vistare incommoda cuncta.
translations.translation: But whatever man prudence of heart leads to enter the cave of Mercury, where he lays down very many goods, of which a very great heap stands, this man can take them for himself with both hands and carry them home; this man can avoid all troubles. (¶19 gives Atwood's interpretive paraphrase, not a translation.)

translations.original: Nescit Sol comitis non memor esse sui
translations.translation: The Sun knows not how to be unmindful of its companion.

translations.original: Ignire ignis amat, non aurificare sed, aurum.
translations.translation: Fire loves fire, say they, not to make gold, but to assimilate it.

translations.original: Intellectus naturam habens subtilem ad intelligendum res intelligibles, participat, cum entibus intensis et cum entibus extensis, viz., cum intenso calore corporis, cum quo conjunctus est et cum intense bonitate sustentata in suis intensis concretis
translations.translation: The intellect, having a subtle nature for understanding intelligible things, participates with intensive beings and with extensive beings, namely with the intense heat of the body with which it is joined, and with the intense goodness sustained in its intense concretes.

threads.note: 'this Light' refers back to a Light discussed before this chunk (the preceding paragraph speaks of the 'fire of life' and 'living light').
'this Reason' refers back to a Reason introduced before this chunk.
Lully, Michael Maier and others: 'to which in the Practice we shall have occasion to allude' (forward reference to the Practice).
The narrow gate 'as in the Mysteries we have already described' (back-reference to the earlier account of the Mysteries).
Atwood says it 'will be necessary... to discuss the point' of the magic action of mind and to 'substantialize... this Intellectual Science' (forward).
'in a former citation from his book to the Athenians, Paracelsus saying, that Separation is the greatest miracle' (back-reference to an earlier citation).
'as before shown, no foreign admixture is allowed to enter' (back-reference).
Separation said to be identical to the ordeals of the Mysteries, 'decomposition and death of the natural life' (links to the earlier Mysteries chapters).
